source.title: Staying awake for dinner: hypothalamic integration of sleep, feeding, and circadian rhythms.

confidence_rationale: Directly supports the metabolic-demand arm of MECH-286: orexin neurons stabilize the sleep-wake switch WHILE driving both wakefulness and foraging for food, integrating sleep with feeding and energy state. This is the biological basis for MECH-286's claim that override (sustained drive under metabolic demand) suppresses sleep onset. Confidence moderate because it is a short conceptual review and the feeding/metabolic coupling is framed as wake-promotion for foraging rather than as a formal gate on offline-mode entry with replay recruitment.
failure_signatures: Orexin's metabolic coupling here promotes wakefulness/foraging under negative energy balance; MECH-286 instead emphasizes high metabolic *demand* (with drive+threat) suppressing sleep onset -- compatible in direction but the review's emphasis is foraging-drive wake-promotion, not threat-gated onset suppression.
As a brief review it provides no causal dissociation isolating a metabolic-demand override on sleep onset from the general orexin wake-drive.

mapping.source_claim_statement: Sleep-wake regulation is inextricably linked to feeding and energy metabolism; the orexin/hypocretin neurons stabilize the flip-flop switch while simultaneously driving wakefulness and foraging for food, with the subparaventricular and dorsomedial hypothalamic nuclei integrating circadian timing into both feeding and wake-sleep patterns.
mapping.ree_translation: Supports MECH-286's metabolic-demand component: that the override authority gating sleep onset is sensitive to metabolic/drive state, not only to threat. Orexin's dual role -- stabilizing wakefulness AND driving foraging under energy demand -- is the biological instantiation of a drive-plus-metabolic signal biasing the switch away from sleep onset.
mapping.mapping_caveat: The review frames metabolic coupling as orexin promoting wakefulness and foraging under negative energy balance, whereas MECH-286 frames metabolic demand (with drive and threat) as suppressing sleep-mode onset. These are the same switch biased the same direction, but the claim's specific 'override suppresses onset and gates replay recruitment' formulation is not what the review tests; the metabolic input is real, the override-and-recruitment packaging is REE's.
mapping.source_context: Conceptual review of hypothalamic integration of sleep, feeding, and circadian rhythms in mammals (rodent-anchored).

confidence_components.notes: Authoritative review by the flip-flop model's originator, focused on the feeding/metabolic-state arm. Mapping fidelity good for the metabolic-demand component of MECH-286; lowered because the framing is foraging-wake-promotion rather than threat-gated onset suppression. Transfer risk moderate.
